section.subsetting_text: Font subsetting removes unused glyphs and characters, keeping only the ones your project actually needs to significantly reduce font file size.
section.steps_title: How to compress a TTF font
section.steps_2: Enter the characters or text you want to keep.
section.steps_3: Choose the output format, such as TTF or WOFF.
section.steps_4: Click Start Compression and download the optimized font.
section.why_text: Large fonts increase page load time, especially on mobile devices or when multiple font files are used. Font compression and subsetting can significantly improve web performance and reduce download size.
section.faq_1_q: What is a font subsetting tool?
section.faq_1_a: A font subsetting tool keeps the characters you actually need and removes the rest to create a smaller font file.
section.faq_2_q: How do I reduce the size of a TTF file?
section.faq_2_a: Upload the TTF file, input the required characters, and generate a subset font to remove unused glyphs and shrink the file size.
section.faq_3_q: Does font subsetting improve web performance?
section.faq_3_a: Yes. Smaller font files mean less downloaded data and faster page loading while keeping the required characters available.
section.faq_4_a: For web delivery, WOFF is often more suitable because it is optimized for browser transfer. Combining WOFF output with font subsetting is a common optimization strategy.
